title: Valmiki gets divine guidance to compile the epic
introduction: Sage Valmiki goes to river Tamasa for a bath and sees a couple of birds, of which a hunter kills one. Valmiki unintentionally utters a poem, which is rich in grammar and new in metre, of which he is very much confused as to why such a poem has come from his tongue. Brahma, the presiding deity of letters appears and ordains Valmiki to author Ramayana, excellent epic of Rama, for which purpose alone he gave such divine meter and grammar to him.
closing: इति वाल्मिकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे द्वितीयः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 2nd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वाक्यविशारदः |
पूजयामास धर्मात्मा सहशिष्यो महामुनिः
verses.iast:
nāradasya tu tadvākyam śrutvā vākya viśāradaḥ |
pūjayāmāsa dharmātmā saha śiśhyo mahāmuniḥ
verses.translation: Then, the great sage Valmiki, a skilled orator and a virtue-minded one, having heard those words of Narada, worshipped him along with disciples.

verses.devanagari:
यथावत्पूजितस्तेन देवर्षिर्नारदस्तथा |
आपृच्छैवाभ्यनुज्ञातः स जगाम विहायसम्
verses.iast:
yathāvat pūjitaḥ tena devarśhiḥ nāradaḥ tathā |
āpṛcchaiva abhyanujJṇātaḥ sa jagāma vihāyasam
verses.translation: That divine sage Narada being worshipped befittingly by Valmiki in that way, on seeking permission of Valmiki to leave and having been permitted by Valmiki, went away heaven-ward.

verses.devanagari:
स मुहूर्तं गते तस्मिन्देवलोकं मुनिस्तदा |
जगाम तमसातीरं जाह्नव्यास्त्वविदूरतः
verses.iast:
sa muhūrtaṃ gate tasmin devalokam muniḥ tadā |
jagāma tamasā tīram jāhnavyāt avidūrataḥ
verses.translation: Then, on Narada's going to the world of gods in a trice, that sage Valmiki went to the banks of Tamasa river not far from Jahnavi river.

glosses.meaning: to the world of gods in a trice
went to the banks of Tamasa river

verses.devanagari:
स तु तीरं समासाद्य तमसाया महामुनिः |
शिष्यमाह स्थितं पार्श्वे दृष्ट्वा तीर्थमकर्दमम्
verses.iast:
sa tu tīram samāsādya tamasāyā muniḥ tadā |
śiśhyam āha sthitam pārśve dṛśhṭvā tīrtham akardamam
verses.translation: Then that sage Valmiki on reaching the shore of the clean Tamasa, and on beholding a ford of that river, spoke to his disciple who was at his side.

verses.devanagari:
अकर्दममिदं तीर्थं भरद्वाज निशामय |
रमणीयं प्रसन्नाम्बु सन्मनुष्यमनो यथा
verses.iast:
akardamam idam tīrtham bharadvāja niśāmaya |
ramaṇīyam prasanna ambu san manuśhya mano yathā
verses.translation: "Oh! Bharadwaja, behold this ford which is without dirt, with clear waters and pleasant like a virtuous man's mind.

verses.devanagari:
न्यस्यतां कलशस्तात दीयतां वल्कलं मम |
इदमेवावगाहिष्ये तमसातीर्थमुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
nyasyatām kalaśaḥ tāta dīyatām valkalam mama |
idam eva avagāhiśhye tamasā tīrtham uttamam
verses.translation: "My dear! Let the hand-vessel [kamaNDalu] be kept [there]. Let my bark-garment be given to me. I will enter this best ford of Tamasa only...

verses.devanagari:
एवमुक्तो भरद्वाजो वाल्मीकेन महात्मना |
प्रायच्छत मुनेस्तस्य वल्कलं नियतो गुरोः
verses.iast:
evam ukto bharadvājo vālmīkena mahātmanā |
prayacchata muneḥ tasya valkalam niyataḥ guroḥ
verses.translation: Thus being said by the great-souled Valmiki, Bharadwaaja who was obedient to his Guru, gave the bark-garment to the sage

glosses.meaning: Bharadwaaja who was obedient towards his Guru

verses.devanagari:
स शिष्यहस्तादादाय वल्कलं नियतेन्द्रियः |
विचचार ह पश्यंस्तत्सर्वतो विपुलं वनम्
verses.iast:
sa śiśhya hastāt ādāya valkalam niyatendriyaḥ |
vicacāra ha paśyan tat sarvato vipulam vanam
verses.translation: That self-controlled Sage Valmiki on taking bark-garment from his disciple's hands, and looking in all directions, indeed moved away from that wide expanse of forest.

verses.devanagari:
तस्याभ्याशे तु मिथुनं चरन्तमनपायिनम् |
ददर्श भगवांस्तत्र क्रौञ्चयोश्चारुनिःस्वनम्
verses.iast:
tasya abhyāśe tu mithunam carantam anapāyinam |
dadarśa bhagavān tatra krauñcayoḥ cāru nisvanam
verses.translation: There holy sage Valmiki saw a couple of curlews, in the vicinity of that river's foreshore, flying there about in togetherness and cooing charmingly.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मात्तु मिथुनादेकं पुमांसं पापनिश्चयः |
जघान वैरनिलयो निषादस्तस्य पश्यतः
verses.iast:
tasmāt tu mithunāt ekam pumāṃsam pāpa niścayaḥ |
jaghāna vairanilayo niśhādaḥ tasya paśyataḥ
verses.translation: A tribal hunter with evil intent, and a receptacle of enimity, killed the male one among the couple of birds, while Valmiki was looking on.

verses.devanagari:
तं शोणितपरीताङ्गं वेष्टमानं महीतले |
भार्या तु निहतं दृष्ट्वा रुराव करुणां गिरम्
वियुक्ता पतिना तेन द्विजेन सहचारिणा |
ताम्रशीर्षेण मत्तेन पत्रिणा सहितेन वै |
verses.iast:
tam śoṇita parītāṇ^gam ceṣṭamānam mahītale |
bhāryā tu nihatam dṛṣṭvā rurāva karuṇām giram
viyuktā patinā tena dvijena sahacāriṇā |
tāmra śīrśheṇa mattena patriṇā sahitena vai |
verses.translation: The wife was moving together with husband with a red crest and with joy, with good wings, always being united with that male bird. On seeing that bird slain on ground reeling with blood covered wings really made wailing sounds with piteous utterances on being separated from her husband.

verses.devanagari:
तथाविधं द्विजं दृष्ट्वा निषादेन निपातितम् |
ऋषेर्धर्मात्मनस्तस्य कारुण्यं समपद्यत
verses.iast:
tathā vidhim dvijam dṛśhṭvā niśhādena nipātitam |
ṛśeḥ dharmātmānaḥ tasya kāruṇyam samapadyata
verses.translation: On seeing that bird felled that way by the tribal hunter, compassion occassioned in that saintly sage Valmiki.

verses.devanagari:
ततः करुणवेदित्वादधर्मोऽयमिति द्विजः |
निशाम्य रुदतीं क्रौञ्चीमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tataḥ karuṇa veditvāt adharmo ayam iti dvijaḥ |
niśāṃya rudatīm krauncīm idam vacanam abraiit
verses.translation: Then on seeing the wailing female krounchi bird, out of state of compassion and apperceiving the killing of male bird as unjust, the sage uttered this sentence...

glosses.meaning: on seeing the wailing Krauncha bird

verses.devanagari:
मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वमगमः शाश्वतीः समाः |
यत् क्रौञ्चमिथुनादेकमवधीः काममोहितम्
verses.iast:
mā niśhāda pratiṣṭhāmtva | magamaḥ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ |
yat krauñca mithunāt eka | mavadhīḥ kāma mohitam
verses.translation: "Oh! violent Hunter, by which reason you have killed one bird of the couple, when it was infatuated by passion, for that reason you will never get a state of rest for everlasting years to come..."
notes: त्वमगमः has been split as tu+ama+gamaH.
'For endless years to come, O Hunter, never shall thy soul find peace /' Romesh C. Dutt.
This verse has many comports of which a few are given hereunder:
This verse is taken as mañgalācaraṇa to Ramayana, for any epic has to have mañgala ādīni; mañgala madhyāni; mañgala antāni A good pious beginning, pious middle and pious ending.
Because this verse has the letter mā at its start and mā is lakṣmī vācaka in Sanskrit. It is ādi varṇaḥ The first letter loka mātā mā ramā mañgala devatā thus amara kośa says for Goddess Lakshmi.

mā= Goddess Lakshmi; niṣāda= Oh! Vishnu [ for Goddess Lakshmi resides in the heart of Vishnu - niṣadīti asmin iti niṣāda ]; yat= by which act; krounca midhunāt = the couple of demons, namely Ravana and Mandodari; kāma mohitam= that impassioned one and stole Seetha; ekam= that one, Ravana; avadhī= you killed; by that act of yours; śaśvatīsamā= everlasting for ages; pratiṣṭām= divine sanctity; tvam agama= you, get.

"Oh, the abode of Goddess Lakshmi, namely oh, Vishnu, by which act of your killing one male demon named Ravana, who in his passion abducted Seetha, and thus you eradicated the vice from the earth, for that you get an everlasting divine sanctity, as Rama, for ages to come."

2] Next niṣāda is attributable to Ravana, because he is the one who tortures others for his benefit. itarām sādayati pīḍayati iti niṣāda thus: Oh! Ravana; krounc midhunāt= from the couple, say Rama and Seetha, who are flying from forest to forest like nest-less birds; ekam= one is, Seetha is; avadhī =you almost killed her by your torture of abducting her; pratiṣṭām= your glory in Lanka, at its zenith, as per the kindness of Brahma; ma agama= never get, hereafter. But this declination is not held right, for it is like a curse, śāpa, and no epic starts with a curse.

3] Next, this verse is said holding Rama in the perspective. Sage Narada gave the details of the legend to Sage Valmiki because Brahma ordered that the legend of Rama is to be recorded. But Ramayana is full of pathos, karuṇa śoka rasa prathāna. If it is to be penned the writer too shall have heart that can outpour that mood. So when Valmiki is at the river banks, Rama, say Vishnu, came in the guise of a tribal, as with other mythological episodes like kirātārjunīya etc., to test the capability of Valmiki in narrating pathos, and killed one bird. Valmiki reacted immediately and Vishnu's test is complete. But in exciting the mood of such holy sage, Vishnu / Rama gets a curse like separation from wife, as below.

niśāda= oh, tribal: Rama to Valmiki / Vishnu to mythology; for your killing one bird of the couple, to the misery of the female one; śāśvatī = as long as you live on this earth; samāḥ pratiṣṭām= togetherness, with your wife; ma agama= do not get.

Oh! Rama, as long as you are on earth, you do not get the love of being together with your wife, because you killed one from the bird couple... and you have to live with your wife departed [to Lanka,] come again, and then departed [to forests.]
But this is differed statement, since Vishnu does not require any personal testing of the capabilities of the writer of Ramayana. Brahma will look after such literary things.

4] The generally accepted meaning of this verse is this. Any epic's gist is to be said at the start or, at its commencement --- kāvya artha sūcanam kascin ādyām eva nirūpyate--- Thus, the above verse included the meaning of whole of the epic, Ramayana.
i] mā niṣāda= Goddess Lakshmi and Vishnu. Their marriage in their incarnations as Rama and Seetha, and Ramayana depicts this in Bala Kanda.

ii] pratiṣṭām tvam agama= renown, you get, by following your father's orders you have repaired to forests, without any political upheaval, thus get an everlasting renown as an obliging son Ayodhya Kanda.
iii] śaśavatī samā= by dwelling in forest and eradicating demons and helping the saints and sages thus, you achieve an everlasting praise Aranaya Kanda.

iv] krouncayoḥ= from the [atrocious] couple; k-- krunca gati kauṭilyā alpī bhāvayoḥ; the atrocious Vali, and Tara couple; ekam kāma mohitam= one, passion, filled, i.e., Vali; avadhii= you killed, you killed Vali Kishkindha Kanda.

v] krounca mithunāt= from the couple of lovely passionate birds here Rama and Seetha; niṣāda that ruffian Ravana, kāma mohitam lustfully, ekamone [i.e., Seetha]; avadhī= almost killed, i.e., her residing in Lanka is as good as death Sundara Kanda.
vi] krounca mithunāt = from the atrocious, couple Ravana and Mandodari; ekam avadhīone Ravana, you killed Yuddha Kanda.

vii] kāma mohitam= by desire, fascinated [ kama also means a longing, desire, let alone lusting]; Seetha is fascinated by her desire to see sage's wives in uttara Ramayana and thus she is sent to forests through Lakshmana. Hence seventh canto, uttara Ramayana is also suggested.

glosses.meaning: [for that reason you] will not get

verses.devanagari:
तस्यैवं ब्रुवतश्चिन्ता बभूव हृदि वीक्षतः |
शोकार्तेनास्य शकुनेः किमिदं व्याहृतं मया
verses.iast:
tasya evam bruvataḥ cintā babhūva hṛdi vīkśataḥ |
śokārtena asya śakuneḥ kim idam vyāhṛtam mayā
verses.translation: Thus speaking and pondering in his heart, he became thoughtful: "What is this utterance by me in grief and anguish for this bird?".

verses.devanagari:
चिन्तयन्स महाप्राज्ञश्चकार मतिमान्मतिम् |
शिष्यञ्चैवाब्रवीद्वाक्यमिदं स मुनिपुङ्गवः
verses.iast:
cintayan sa mahāprājñaḥ cakāra matimān matim |
śiśyam ca eva abravīt vākyam idam sa munipuṇ^gavaḥ
verses.translation: That great wise one who was an intellectual and the best among sages, on cogitating, made up his mind and also spoke these words to the disciple...

verses.devanagari:
पादबद्धोऽक्षरसमस्तन्त्रीलयसमन्वितः |
शोकार्तस्य प्रवृत्तो मे श्लोको भवतु नान्यथा
verses.iast:
pāda baddhaḥ akśara samaḥ tantrī laya samanvitaḥ |
śokārtasya pravṛtto me śloko bhavatu na anyathā
verses.translation: "While I was tormented by grief, there arose a sentence consisting of four verses possessing metrically posited letters suitable to be played as song and string music and that will be called Shloka, not otherwise..."
notes: This verse he uttered is in four quarters, each quarter with equally posited eight syllables. This is called anuṣṭubhmetre in Sanskrit poetry. The eight syllables are, -- mā ni ṣā da pra ti ṣṭāñ tva | ma ga ma śā śva tīḥ sa mā --Each quarter is pādain Sanskrit, pedein Latin; with two quarters in first stanza, and two stanzas one verse. This apart there are other rules like caesura yati; alliteration prāsa; and other compositional rules. It has come out of śokasorrow, so the format is named as sloka. And, ślokaalso means yaśas, kīrtirenown.

glosses.meaning: while I was tormented by grief
[suitable for] union of song and string music

verses.devanagari:
शिष्यस्तु तस्य ब्रुवतो मुनेर्वाक्यमनुत्तमम् |
प्रतिजग्राह संतुष्टस्तस्य तुष्टोऽभवद्मुनिः
verses.iast:
śiṣyaḥ tu tasya bruvato muner vākyam anuttamam |
prati jagrāha santuśhṭaḥ tasya tuṣṭoaḥ abhavat muniḥ
verses.translation: Even the disciple happily received what that is articulated by the saint, a unique articulation, by which the saint too, became happy.

verses.devanagari:
सोऽभिषेकं ततः कृत्वा तीर्थे तस्मिन् यथाविधि |
तमेव चिन्तयन्नर्थमुपावर्तत वै मुनिः
verses.iast:
so'bhiṣekam tataḥ kṛtvā tīrthe tasmin yathāvidhi |
tam eva cintayan artham upāvartata vai muniḥ
verses.translation: Then that saint on performing his bathing in that ford according to custom, and still thinking on the purport of his utterance, he returned towards his hermitage.
notes: This is mid day bath for these hermits. tato madhyāhna snānārtham mṛdam āharet | - - prekṣya sa omkāram ādityam triḥ nimajje jalāśaye - - vyāsa smṛtiThe word abhiśekarefers to ceremonial showering of waters on deities or on kings in his coronation. At the beginning Valmiki arrives at the river for a daily bath, which he would do by usual dipping in river waters. But here it appears that waters are showered on him, abhiśekam kṛtvameaning that waters showered on him are on the analogy of poetic verses of Ramayana.

glosses.meaning: back, he came, really [returned to hermitage.]

verses.devanagari:
भरद्वाजस्ततः शिष्यो विनीतः श्रुतवान् गुरोः |
कलशं पूर्णमादाय पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम ह
verses.iast:
bharadvājaḥ tataḥ śiṣyo vinītaḥ śrutavān guroḥ |
kalaśam pūrṇamādāya pṛśhṭhataḥ anujagāma ha
verses.translation: Then Bharadwaja, the obedient disciple and an erudite scholar, for he heard and learnt many scriptures by listening, on taking handy-vessel full with water followed at the behind of his mentor.

glosses.meaning: one who listened many scriptures, [erudite scholar]

verses.devanagari:
स प्रविश्याश्रमपदं शिष्येण सह धर्मवित् |
उपविष्टः कथाश्चान्याश्चकार ध्यानमास्थितः
verses.iast:
sa praviśya āśrama padam śiṣyeṇa saha dharmavit |
upaviśhṭaḥ kathāḥ ca anyāḥ cakāra dhyānamāsthitaḥ
verses.translation: He that knower of dharma, Valmiki, having entered the threshold of hermitage along with disciples, and having seated spoke about the day-to-day teachings and also other things, but he himself is preoccupied in cogitation on the verse.

glosses.meaning: other, topics, also, made - spoke about

verses.devanagari:
आजगाम ततो ब्रह्म लोककर्ता स्वयं प्रभुः |
चतुर्मुखो महातेजा द्रष्टुं तं मुनिपुङ्गवम्
verses.iast:
ājagāma tataḥ brahmo lokakartā svayam prabhuḥ |
catur mukho mahātejā draṣṭum tam munipuṇ^gavam
verses.translation: Then, the great resplendent Four-faced creator of fourteen worlds, almighty Brahma, arrived there on his own, to see that eminent saint Valmiki.
notes: Comment; The deities do not usually arrive on their own, but reveal themselves after a great penance, or on raising hue and cry as is done by demon devotees. Here Brahma, one among the Trinity of Hindu mythology, arrives on his own, to execute a divine deed through Valmiki, i.e. authoring the epic, Ramayana.

verses.devanagari:
वाल्मीकिरथ तं दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थाय वाग्यतः |
प्राञ्जलिः प्रयतो भूत्वा तस्थौ परमविस्मितः
verses.iast:
vālmīkiḥ atha tam dṛṣṭvā sahasā utthāya vāgyataḥ |
prānjaliḥ prayato bhūtvā tasthau parama vismitaḥ
verses.translation: Then that pious saint Valmiki is highly surprised on seeing Brahma, and on quickly getting up from his seat with his palms adjoined humbly, he stood aside, as he is spellbind.

verses.devanagari:
पूजयामास तं देवं पाद्यार्घ्यासनवन्दनैः |
प्रणम्य विधिवच्चैनं पृष्ट्वानामयमव्ययम्
verses.iast:
pūjayāmāsa tam devam pādya arghya āsana vandanaiḥ |
praṇaṃya vidhivat ca enam pṛśhṭvā ca eva nirāmayam
verses.translation: Valmiki venerated Brahma, on inquiring into his well-being, washed his feet, drenched his thirst, seated him to rest, and adored at best with customarily obeisance.
notes: Comment: Brahma is one in the Trinity of Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva. Brahma is pictured to have four faces, each representing one Veda, where Vedas are four in number. He is the creator of worlds, while Vishnu maintains them, and Shiva dissolute them. The concert of Brahma is Saraswati, the presiding deity of speech, who was earlier requested by Brahma to be on the tongue of Valmiki to utter the poem, [as at 1-2-15] as an intuition to Valmiki. Thus Brahma now arrives to ordain Valmiki to author Ramayana.

glosses.meaning: him, such a one, at that god

verses.devanagari:
अथोपविश्य भगवानासने परमार्चिते |
वाल्मीकये च ऋषये सन्दिदेशासनं ततः
verses.iast:
atha upaviśya bhagavān āsane parama arcite |
vālmīkaye ca ṛṣaye sandideśa āsanam tataḥ
verses.translation: Then god Brahma, who is seated on a high seat, very highly worshipped by Valmiki, also beckoned at Valmiki to take a seat.

verses.devanagari:
ब्रह्मणा समनुज्ञातः सोऽप्युपाविशदासने |
उपविष्टे तदा तस्मिन्साक्षाल्लोकपितामहे |
तद्गतेनैव मनसा वाल्मीकिर्ध्यानमास्थितः ||
verses.iast:
brahmaṇā samanujñātaḥ so'pi upāviśat āsane |
upaviṣṭe tadā tasmin sākśāt loka pitāmahe |
tat gatena eva manasā vālmīkiḥ dhyānam āsthitaḥ ||
verses.translation: Even though Valmiki sat on his seat when duly permitted by Brahma, and though the Grandparent of the worlds is manifestly sitting before him, but the same broodings on those happenings occurred on that day have recurred on his mind. [1-2-27-28a]

verses.devanagari:
पापात्मना कृतं कष्टं वैरग्रहणबुद्धिना |
यस्तादृशं चारुरवं क्रौञ्चं हन्यादकारणात् ||
verses.iast:
pāpātmanā kṛtam kaṣṭam vaira grahaṇa buddhinā |
yat tādṛśam cāruravam krauncam hanyāt akāraṇāt ||
verses.translation: "He that tribal hunter, who killed a cutely calling krounch bird for no good reason than intending to capture the kill, is an evil souled one that caused hardship..." [1-2-28b-29a]

verses.devanagari:
शोचन्नेव मुहुः क्रौञ्चीमुपश्लोकमिमं पुनः |
जगावन्तर्गतमना भूत्वा शोकपरायणः ||
verses.iast:
śocan eva punaḥ krauncīm upa ślokam imam jagau |
punar antargata manā bhūtvā śoka parāyaṇaḥ ||
verses.translation: Remaining in melancholic mood Valmiki turned his mind to the depth of thinking, and again thinking only on the krouncha bird he sung the same verse, involuntarily. [1-2-29b-30a]
notes: The word jaguḥis singing; gai= śabde; liṭ; prathama bahu; jagau - jagatuḥ - jaguḥ; variant of gāy; c.f. Raghuvamsha of Kalidasa, verse 20, in fourth sarga; ākumārakathoddhātaṃ śāligopyo jaguryaśaḥ

glosses.meaning: depths of, mind, on turning in
about krouncha bird, on thinking, only

verses.devanagari:
तमुवाच ततो ब्रह्मा प्रहसन्मुनिपुङ्गवम् |
श्लोक एव त्वया बद्धो नात्र कार्या विचारणा
verses.iast:
tam uvāca tato brahmā prahasan munipuṅgavam |
śloka evāstvayām baddho na atra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
verses.translation: Then, Brahma smilingly spoke to that eminent saint Valmiki, "But, what that is composed is a verse only... and there is no need to think through... [1-2-30b-31a]

glosses.meaning: to him, that saint, the eminent, spoke to
not, there, need to, think through.

verses.devanagari:
मच्छन्दादेव ते ब्रह्मन् प्रवृत्तेयं सरस्वती |
रामस्य चरितं सर्वं कुरु त्वमृषिसत्तम
verses.iast:
mat cchandāt eva te brahman pravṛtte ayam sarasvatī |
rāmasya caritam kṛtsnam kuru tvam ṛśhisattama |
verses.translation: "Oh, Brahman, that speech of yours sprang forth at my wish alone, hence oh, eminent sage, you shall render the legend of Rama, in its entirety... [1-2-31b-32a]

verses.devanagari:
धर्मात्मनो गुणवतो लोके रामस्य धीमतः |
वृत्तं कथय धीरस्य यथा ते नारदाच्छ्रुतम्
verses.iast:
dharmātmano bhagavato loke rāmasya dhīmataḥ
vṛttam kathaya dhīrasya yathā te nāradāt śrutam |
verses.translation: "You shall narrate the legend of Rama, the virtuous, intellectual and an intrepid one, and a godlike person in this world as well, as you have heard it from sage Narada. [1-2-32b-33a]

glosses.meaning: by you, as heard, from Narada

verses.devanagari:
रहस्यं च प्रकाशं च यद् वृत्तं तस्य धीमतः |
रामस्य सहसौमित्रे राक्षसानां च सर्वशः
वैदेह्याश्चापि यद् वृत्तं प्रकाशं यदि वा रहः |
तच्चाप्यविदितं सर्वं विदितं ते भविष्यति
verses.iast:
rahasyam ca prakāśam ca yad vṛttam tasya dhīmataḥ
rāmasya saha saumitre rākśasānām ca sarvaśaḥ |
vaidehyāḥ ca eva yad vṛttam prakāśam yadi vā rahaḥ
tat ca api aviditam sarvam viditam te bhaviṣyati |
verses.translation: "The adventures of valorous Rama along with Lakshmana, and the misadventures of demons, known or unknown in every detail, and even the plight of Vaidehi which is either revealed or un-revealed so far, and whatever legend that has happened, all that will also be known to you, even if it were to be unknown, as yet... [1-2-33b-35a]

glosses.meaning: which is, the plight, of Vaidehi, also, even
all, to you, known, it will be.

verses.devanagari:
न ते वागनृता काव्ये काचिदत्र भविष्यति |
कुरु रामकथां पुण्यां श्लोकबद्धां मनोरमाम्
verses.iast:
na te vāk anṛtā kāvye kācit atra bhaviśhyati
kuru rāma kathām puṇyām śloka baddhām manoramām |
verses.translation: "You shall versify the heart pleasing and merit-yielding legend of Rama, and not a single word of yours will be unfounded in this epic... [1-2-35b-36a]

verses.devanagari:
यावत्स्थास्यन्ति गिरयः सरितश्च महीतले |
तावद्रामायणकथा लोकेषु प्रचरिष्यति
verses.iast:
yāvat sthāsyanti girayaḥ saritaḥ ca mahītale
tāvat rāmāyaṇa kathā lokeṣu pracariṣyati |
verses.translation: "As long as the mountains and even rivers flourish on the surface of the earth, so long the legend of Ramayana will flourish in this world... [1-2-36b-37a]

verses.devanagari:
यावद्रामायणकथा त्वत्कृता प्रचरिष्यति |
तावदूर्ध्वमधश्च त्वं मल्लोकेषु निवत्स्यसि |
verses.iast:
yāvat rāmasya ca kathā tvat kṛtā pracariśhyati |
tāvat ūrdhvam adhaḥ ca tvam mat lokeśhu nivatsyasi |
verses.translation: "And as long as Rama's legend authored by you flourishes...till then you will flourish in heavenly, in netherworlds, and even in my abode, namely Abode of Brahma...

verses.devanagari:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् ब्रह्मा तत्रैवान्तरधीयत |
ततः सशिष्यो भगवान्मुनिर्विस्मयमाययौ
verses.iast:
iti uktvā bhagavān brahmā tatra eva antaradhīyata |
tataḥ sa śiśhyo bhagavān muniḥ vismayam āyayau
verses.translation: On saying thus that Divinity Brahma vanished then and there only, and then that godly sage Valmiki came by astonishment, along with his disciples. [1-2-38b-c]

verses.devanagari:
तस्य शिष्यास्ततः सर्वे जगुः श्लोकमिमं पुनः |
मुहुर्महुः प्रीयमाणाः प्राहुश्च भृशविस्मिताः
verses.iast:
tasya śiśhyāḥ tataḥ sarve jaguḥ ślokam imam punaḥ |
muhur muhuḥ prīyamāṇāḥ prāhuḥ ca bhṛśa vismitāḥ
verses.translation: Then all of the disciples of Valmiki sang this verse time and again very delightedly, and muchstonished they also recited this verse, reciprocally.

verses.devanagari:
समाक्षरैश्चतुर्भिर्यः पादैर्गीतो महर्षिणा |
सोऽनुव्याहरणाद् भूयः श्लोकः श्लोकत्वमागतः
verses.iast:
samākśaraiḥ caturbhiḥ yaḥ pādaiḥ gīto maharśhiṇā |
saḥ anuvyāharaṇāt bhūyaḥ śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ
verses.translation: Equally lettered, four-footed is that verse when great Sage Valmiki articulated it, and when repetitively recited by one and all, it attained prominence as verse proper.
notes: Comment: A poet never says poetry to satisfy his own instincts, but to imbue an involuntary imagination or passion in oComment: A poet never says poetry to satisfy his own instincts, but to imbue an involuntary imagination or passion in others when read or heard by the so called others. It is the empathy of that poetry. For Kalidasa it is śṛngara, passion, for Bhavabhuti it is pity 'eko rasaḥ karuṇa...' for Valmiki it is pathos, shoka. For this Kavi Kalidas says: niṣāda viddha aṇḍaja darśanotthaḥ ślokatvam āpadyata yasya śokaḥ -- raghu vañśa 14-60 There are two texts for this one is, ślokaḥ ślokatam āgataḥ... meaning that the verse originally structured metrically can now can be sung. Second is śokaḥ ślokatvam āgataḥ... the pathos of the poet attained the status of verse that is now being sung by the disciples, thus anyone can recite it.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य बुद्धिरियं जाता महर्षेर्भावितात्मनः |
कृत्स्नं रामायणं काव्यमीदृशैः करवाण्यहम्
verses.iast:
tasya buddhiḥ iyam jātā maharṣeḥ bhāvitātmanaḥ |
kṛtsnam rāmāyaṇam kāvyam īdṛśaiḥ karavāṇyaham
verses.translation: Born is an intuition in that great sage and contemplated soul asserting that "I will compose entire Ramayana, the epic, in suchlike verses...'

glosses.meaning: kR^itsnam raamaayaNam kaavyam = entire, Ramayana, epic

verses.devanagari:
उदारवृत्तार्थपदैर्मनोरमैः
तदास्य रामस्य चकार कीर्तिमान् |
समाक्षरैः श्लोकशतैर्यशस्विनो
यशस्करं काव्यमुदारधीर्मुनिः
verses.iast:
udāra vṛtta artha padaiḥ manoramaiḥ
tadā asya rāmasya cakāra kīrtimān |
sama akśaraiḥ śloka śataiḥ yaśasvino
yaśaskaram kāvyam udāra darśanaḥ
verses.translation: That celebrated sage and magnanimous seer Valmiki then authored the highly renowned Rama's legend extolling Rama's renown, with symmetrically worded verses, and words versified to yield meanings semantically, prosody free-flowing, and with hundreds of such verses.

glosses.meaning: of that highly renowned one, Rama
with symmetrical, letters, verses, in hundreds

verses.devanagari:
तदुपगतसमाससन्धियोगं
सममधुरोपनतार्थवाक्यबद्धम् |
रघुवरचरितं मुनिप्रणीतं
दशशिरसश्च वधं निशामयध्वम्
verses.iast:
tad upagata samāsa sandhi yogam
sama madhuropanata artha vākya baddham |
raghuvara caritam munipraṇītam
daśa śirasaḥ ca vadham niśāmaya adhvam
verses.translation: That epic contains uncomplicated compounds, conjunctions and conjugations, and has expressive sentences that are well knit and led evenly and sweetly, and that legend pertains to the best one from Raghu's dynasty, namely Rama, which also includes the extermination of the Ten headed evil named Ravana, and further, it is said by the sage, hence this may now be listened…
notes: This is balladeers bidding to the audience. The word muni praṇītamreminds that a non-saint cannot tell an epic; na anṛśi kurute kāvyamand hence it is to be listened attentively.

glosses.itrans: sama madhura upanata artha vaakya baddham
glosses.iast: sama madhura upanata artha vākya baddham
glosses.devanagari: सम मधुर उपनत अर्थ वाक्य बद्धं
glosses.meaning: evenly, sweetly, led, expressive, sentences, well-knit
